intro: Personal care supports intimate everyday tasks like washing, dressing and toileting; how you help shows the respect and dignity you give.
points: Always gain consent before and during personal care; if a person withdraws it, stop, even mid-task.
Protect privacy and dignity by closing doors, covering the body and uncovering only the area you are caring for.
Hand hygiene is the single most important way to prevent infection; use fresh single-use gloves and aprons for each task.
Report unexplained bruising, injury or a frightened person straight away as a possible safeguarding concern.
Report redness that does not fade when pressed as a possible pressure ulcer; never massage the area.
Support independence, offer real choice, follow the care plan, and write down any changes you notice.
